steps.prompt: New quest: read {quest} (and the code and docs it cites; the MuJoCo API is node_modules/@mujoco/mujoco/mujoco.d.ts). Write the spec to {run}/spec.md following your role card: numbered test cases with hand-checked expected values (body/joint/actuator counts and masses for both species, the reflex math cases with hand-worked Jacobians, and how mj_jacBody's arrays are passed in these bindings (check it in Node in your scratchpad)), the species file shape, the namespaces and who-touches-what table, and how the spike fits pm.motion's controller pattern. Reply when it's written.

prompt.un-automate-monde: Spec: {run}/spec.md (quest: {quest}). Implement it in the source and data files the spec assigns the builder, and nothing else. Run .crew/gate.sh before replying.
prompt.le-testeur: Spec: {run}/spec.md (quest: {quest}). Write its test cases in the test file(s) the spec assigns the tester, and nothing else, including the real-MuJoCo Node test (load MuJoCo with js/require as test/pm/creature_mujoco_test.cljs does). The builder is coding in parallel.

steps.prompt: Run the gate (.crew/gate.sh) and write the gate note to {run}/gate-note.md as your role card says.

Review the round's changes against {run}/spec.md and {quest}: git diff for edited files, and read the new files (git status lists them). Check: nothing in code names a species or body (grep src for horse|dog|pony|juniper|neck|head outside data and docstrings); the reflex math is pure and matches the spec's formula; reflex joints really leave the twitch noise; arrays passed to mj_jacBody are allocated once, not per step; MuJoCo objects still freed on failure; the real-MuJoCo test really drops each species on its side and checks clearance and up-axis; the ?pony flag still leaves the normal game untouched. Write the review to {run}/review.md (at most 5 ranked findings).
